headline: Make everyday work

lead: I help small service businesses organize information, responsibilities, and workflows — then improve them with practical tools and automation where needed.

servicesIntro: Start with one part of the business that keeps getting stuck. I work with small service teams, typically 2–15 people.
services: Messages arrive through several channels, and follow-up depends on someone remembering.
Give each inquiry one record, a responsible person, and a next action.
Important files and details are spread across email, chats, folders, and spreadsheets.
Decide what belongs where and make the current version easy to find.
Tasks pass between people without a clear owner or next step.
Make handoffs explicit so everyone can see who does what and when.
Tools, reminders, or automations stop working as expected.
Find where work breaks, fix the affected step, and make failures visible.
The team keeps checking statuses, requesting the same details, or chasing updates.
Remove repeat work and automate predictable steps where it helps.
servicesEnd: If you’re starting from scratch, we can set up a simple workflow for the requests or jobs you need to handle first.
method: Start with one real example. Find out where work stalls and agree on what needs to change.
Give information a home and make ownership, statuses, and rules clear.
Repair or build the smallest useful tool. Use automation or AI only where it serves a clear purpose.
Test a normal case and an exception, agree on what to do when things go wrong, and leave clear instructions.
aboutBody: I’m Aleks Karpov. My work combines hands-on operations, managing small teams, and making administrative processes easier to run. I’ve worked with HR and payroll processes, and I build practical tools with Google Workspace and Apps Script when they fit the job.
aboutFocus: I focus on making processes easier to follow, documenting how they work, and making it clear what to do when something stops.
contactLead: You don't need a detailed specification. Just describe what's difficult, unreliable, or taking too much manual effort.
